A ruling that could reshape rosters heading into 2027. #CollegeSoftball

article.headline: 5-for-5 Eligibility Litigation Reaches the Tenth Circuit: What It Means for College Softball

research.facts:
5-for-5 Eligibility Litigation Update
**Source:** joneswalker.com / si.com / morganlewis.com / steptoe.com
**Confidence:** HIGH
- NCAA 5-for-5 (Five-for-Five) eligibility rule adopted June 23, 2026
- Rule gives athletes five years of eligibility starting when they enroll or the academic year following their 19th birthday, whichever comes first
- Challenge: Wisne v. NCAA (filed in Colorado federal court)
- July 31, 2026: Judge Charlotte N. Sweeney granted preliminary injunction for class of 2022 athletes
- Court clarified ruling does not enjoin NCAA's roster limit, transfer, and related rules
- NCAA appealed to Tenth Circuit and sought a stay
- August 21, 2026: Stay granted pending appeal
- October 13, 2026: Tenth Circuit heard arguments
- Softball impact: If NCAA loses, teams may be able to add former players from class of 2022 — assuming they remain under roster caps
- Related state-level suits also pending across the country
